subject: hospital thermometer heat
title: What If Your Fever Hit 115 Degrees? One Man's Did, and He Walked Out

scenes.text: What if your body temperature hit 115 degrees? One man's did. He lived.
Normal is 98.6 Fahrenheit. Above 104, or 40 Celsius, doctors call it life-threatening: the enzymes that run your cells start to fail.
Atlanta, July 10th, 1980, in a heat wave: 90 degrees and humid. Willie Jones, 52, collapsed with heatstroke.
At Grady Memorial Hospital his temperature read 115.7 Fahrenheit, 46.5 Celsius. Hotter than any survivor ever recorded.
Past that line, the organs that burn the most energy go first, the heart and the brain: unconsciousness, organ failure, death.
Jones spent 24 days in hospital and was discharged. Guinness still lists him. Nobody has beaten the record, and nobody wants to.

description:
What if your body temperature hit 115 degrees Fahrenheit? On 10 July 1980, during an Atlanta heat wave, 52-year-old Willie Jones was admitted to Grady Memorial Hospital with heatstroke and a body temperature of 46.5 C (115.7 F), the highest ever recorded in a survivor.
Body temperatures above 40 C (104 F) are life-threatening: enzymes begin to denature, and the organs with the highest energy demand, the heart and brain, fail first. The air that day was about 32 C with 44 percent humidity. Jones was discharged after 24 days. This is a historical record, not medical advice; heatstroke is an emergency.
